title: The Wrong Tide
_designNote: Drowned Coast chain 5. 7 beats, 6 terminals. Two 'good' terminals (redirected vs diplomatic) reward different investigation routes. allowUnderflow=false — this chain has no removeItem effects, so strict mode is fine.

beats.description: At Kelpholm's Rider post, Postmaster Dann lays out the commission: 'Tide's three hours off, every third day. Find out why. Pilgrims say omen. I say something big is moving down there.'
Three obvious reads: ask the pilgrims, survey the tide mechanically, or force the issue and draw something up from the deep.

choices.text: Light a fire-signal at the shore. Force a surfacing.

beats.description: The pilgrims speak of a 'below-song' — a rhythmic low-frequency sound from the deep. They beg the player not to dive. 'It is maintenance,' the eldest says. 'Not malice. Not yet.'

choices.text: Nod and move on. Make no promise.

beats.description: The off-cycle is mechanically regular: volume displacement suggests a large sub-surface reroute. Something is being built, not thrashed.
Time to close. Three routes remain.

choices.text: Signal for a Fairgean parley — respectfully.
Report what you have. Do not close.

beats.description: The fire-signal burns green. Three minutes. Six. Then the surface breaks and a Fairgean speaker rises — hostile.
Thirty feet down, a Tide-Eater — a Fairgean maintenance-beast — is rerouting a deep current as nest construction. It notices you.

choices.text: Redirect the current. Spare the beast.

beats.description: The Fairgean speaker surfaces unhurried. 'We are building. You are an interruption. Speak.' Your measurements matter here.

choices.text: Propose a shared maintenance window. Tide predictability for peace.

beats.description: The speaker is braced for ambush. Your next move decides the shape of the conversation.
Dann shrugs. 'Another rider, then.' The commission sits on the board for anyone else. Chain closed without progress.
You hand in a partial report. Dann pays half — the work counts. The commission stays open for next arc.
You run. The shore behind you goes green, then dark. The pilgrims do not meet your eye on the way home.
The Tide-Eater dies loud. Tide is restored. A current you never saw goes slack, and something far down makes a noise that is not a song.
You route the beast around the shore. It works, eyes on you the whole time. Tide restored. The pilgrims weep with relief.
You walk away with a Fairgean translator's mark pressed into your palm. The tide keeps its new rhythm, but predictably now. A door has opened you did not know existed.
